sections.changelog:
Added

  • **New relevance setting «Product type first» (Relevance tab, off by default).** Among matches with equal query coverage, it prefers a product whose title *starts* with what was searched for over one that merely mentions it further along. Catalogs name the thing first and qualify it after, so "Дисплей iPhone 13" is a screen while "Проклейка дисплея iPhone 13" is an adhesive for one — both match the same words, and plain relevance regularly ranks the accessory first. The reason is inverse document frequency working against a mixed-language catalog: when the modules themselves are listed as "LCD" (1510 products) the word "дисплей" survives almost only in accessory titles (83 products), which makes it rare and therefore heavy, so the accessory wins on the shopper's own word. Comparison runs on the coverage-group stems, so a synonym counts — a search for "screen" recognizes a title that opens with "LCD". Titles that open with a brand or an article number never earn the flag, so such catalogs keep their existing order. Measured on a 13k-product parts catalog: 4 of 14 sample queries corrected, the other 10 byte-identical, +13 ms per query.
